description:
Walk crates/*/, read each Cargo.toml package name, record whether docs/api.md, README.md and CLAUDE.md exist and their byte sizes.

TOKEN ESTIMATOR. KOVAN has no tokenizer and must not gain one (offline/deterministic, no ML). Estimate as ceil(chars/4) and DOCUMENT IT AS AN ESTIMATE everywhere it is printed -- never call it a token count. Print bytes alongside so the maintainer can sanity-check. The chars/4 ratio is a convention for English+code, and technical markdown with heavy punctuation and identifiers runs denser, so the estimate is optimistic; treat the budget as soft and say so in the output.
title: agent-docs: crate inventory + token estimator

description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'the turbine blades are reaction + impulse. They are angled differently at each stage. Have placeholder angles for those. When detailed turbine design lands (and it should later), then take the angulation from the physical turbine model.'

INTERIM (done under op-wqk.14.3): stator + rotor blades are drawn with a PLACEHOLDER per-stage angle schedule. These are illustrative only and MUST be labelled as such in the doc comments -- they are not derived from any turbine design and must never be presented as if they were.

THE PHYSICS THEY STAND IN FOR:
  - Degree of reaction is the fraction of the stage enthalpy drop taken across the ROTOR. Impulse ~ 0% (all expansion in the fixed nozzle/stator, rotor just turns the flow); reaction typically ~50% (expansion split between stator and rotor).
  - Classic steam-turbine practice puts impulse stages at the HP inlet (Rateau/Curtis) and reaction stages toward the LP exhaust (Parsons), so a multi-stage machine is a MIXTURE and the blade angles vary stage by stage -- which is exactly why one fixed angle for all rows is wrong.
  - The blade SHAPES differ too, not just the angles: impulse rotor blades are near-symmetric buckets; reaction blades are asymmetric aerofoils. If the drawing is to distinguish stage types honestly, shape should follow angle.

WHEN THIS IS DONE: the angles must come from the real turbine model rather than the placeholder schedule -- stator exit angle alpha and rotor inlet/outlet angles beta per stage, plus the degree of reaction per stage. That model does not exist yet; it arrives with the detailed turbine design work (see op-dt3.18, the TampinesSteamArray-coupled turbine). Wire the dependency and delete the placeholder schedule at that point; do not leave both paths live.
title: TurbineVisual: per-stage blade angulation from the physical turbine model (replace placeholders)

description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop. NOT fixed -- it needs a change to the pressure-equation formulation.

SYMPTOM. The array's stored mass Sum(rho*V) falls by more than the boundary mass fluxes account for whenever there is strong volumetric heating, and the transient global energy balance fails by the enthalpy of exactly that missing mass.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, prescribed 1.0 g/s inlet, 200 W uniform source, dt 2e-4 s, 4000 steps = 0.8 s, after a 200-step flow warm-up):
  energy: integral(mdot_in*h_in - mdot_out*h_out + Q) dt = 9.5696 J   vs   d(Sum rho*V*h) = 0.1125 J   -> residual 9.4571 J = 5.9 % of the 160 J delivered
  mass:   integral(mdot_in - mdot_out) dt = 2.761e-7 kg               vs   d(Sum rho*V) = -2.556e-5 kg -> residual 2.584e-5 kg
  ratio:  9.4571 J / 2.584e-5 kg = 366.1 kJ/kg, inside the 311.20-511.2 kJ/kg range the field spans.
So the two residuals are ONE event: the energy that fails to balance is the enthalpy carried by the mass that fails to balance.

CAUSE. step() computes a continuity density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi), then correct_thermo OVERWRITES self.rho with the EOS density rho(p,h). The pressure equation reconciles them only through its compressibility diagonal psi*V/dt with psi = drho/dp|_h. It carries NO drho/dh|_p term, so the density drop caused by HEATING is never fed back as mass the domain must expel.

RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT (this is why the cause above is the remaining explanation):
- Not the outlet boundary flux (op-nnqi). Residual unchanged at 9.4571 J by the boundary pressure-correction fix that cut the STEADY boundary residual 113-fold (1.3834 W -> 0.0122 W).
- Not spatial truncation. 9.37 J at n=8, 9.43 J at n=16, 8.65 J at n=32 -- flat under refinement.
- Not an unconverged PIMPLE loop. Identical at 1/2/4/8 outer correctors (9.4571 / 9.4796 / 9.4795 / 9.4795 J; converged by 2). This was a stated prediction and the measurement FALSIFIED it -- recorded here so nobody re-derives the same wrong guess.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS. The enthalpy-driven density change must enter the pressure equation, e.g. an explicit (drho/dh|_p)*(h - h_old)/dt mass source alongside the psi*V/dt diagonal, or a genuinely coupled rho update. That is a pEqn formulation change and was deliberately not slipped in alongside a boundary-condition fix. Note the STEADY balance is unaffected and closes to 0.006 % of Q -- this only bites in a transient with significant density change.

REGRESSION TEST (characterises rather than hides it; asserts the two residuals are the same event, so it fails if anything ELSE starts breaking the balance):
  openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::lateral_coupling::tests::transient_energy_imbalance_is_the_enthalpy_of_the_unconserved_mass

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables' TampinesSteamArray shares this pEqn verbatim.
title: OPCPFluidArray pEqn: compressibility carries drho/dp but no drho/dh -- EOS mass unconserved under strong heating
